title: Newman: running the collection on the command line and in the pipeline

videos.script: A collection you run by hand is only as good as the day you remember to run it. {{remember}} This lesson takes the collection out of Postman. Newman runs it from a terminal, with no window and no account. {{newman}} You install it into the project with npm, at one exact version, and give the run a short name. {{install}} Then you read what a run prints. Every request, every test, and a table that counts them. {{table}} When a test fails, Newman says which, and why, and exits with code one. {{fail}} That number is what a pipeline listens to. Zero means go on. Anything else means stop. Newman can also write the result as files. A JUnit file for the pipeline, and JSON for anything else. {{reports}} Last, the pipeline itself. A GitHub Actions workflow starts boxoffice, waits for it, runs the collection and keeps the report. {{pipeline}} You run the same steps on your own machine first, so you know they work before a server does. {{local}}
